title: [HIGH] Git clone exposes private child resources with only pod-root Read
description:
**File:** [`crates/solid-pod-rs-server/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/solid-pod-rs/blob/fix/acl-candidate-control/blob/fix/crates/solid-pod-rs-server/src/lib.rs#L4792-L4017) (lines 4792, 4797, 4816, 4017)
**Project:** solid-pod-acl-control
**Severity:** HIGH  •  **Confidence:** high  •  **Slug:** `acl-check`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `noreply@anthropic.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

handle_git (git smart-HTTP, clone/fetch) authorises the request by calling enforce_read_ctx on the pod-root container path `/{pod}/` only (lines 4792-4799), then hands the entire repository to GitHttpService::handle (4816) which serves all committed objects via upload-pack. But every LDP PUT/POST/PATCH to a git-backed pod is committed into `data_root/{pod}/.git` by git_mark_write (4008-4023), and solid-pod-rs-git/src/mark.rs:168-180 does `git add -- <path>` + `git commit` for each written resource individually — including resources that live under a restrictive child ACL (e.g. `/{pod}/private/*`). A pod root is very commonly Read-public because it hosts `/profile/card`. Consequently any caller granted Read on the pod root (often anonymous) can `git clone` the pod and read every resource ever written under more restrictive child ACLs, completely bypassing per-resource WAC. Worse, because git history is append-only, resources remain clonable even after their ACL is later tightened or the resource is deleted via LDP. This is a second serving path (the git tree) that does not honour the per-resource ACL the LDP GET path (enforce_read_ctx) enforces.

## Recommendation

Either (a) enforce Read on each object/path served by upload-pack against its effective ACL before streaming, or (b) do not commit resources governed by a child ACL into a repository that is served wholesale on pod-root Read — scope the served repo to only resources whose ACL matches the pod-root grant. At minimum, deny anonymous/pod-root-only callers from cloning when any descendant has a more restrictive ACL.

title: [HIGH_BUG] Web-Ledger fee debited before the request is validated or served
description:
**File:** [`crates/solid-pod-rs-server/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/solid-pod-rs/blob/fix/acl-candidate-control/blob/fix/crates/solid-pod-rs-server/src/lib.rs#L1017-L2923) (lines 1017, 1742, 1461, 1629, 2923)
**Project:** solid-pod-acl-control
**Severity:** HIGH_BUG  •  **Confidence:** high  •  **Slug:** `other-value-loss`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `noreply@anthropic.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

enforce_write_ctx/enforce_read_inner debit the caller's Web Ledger inside the authorisation gate via charge_granted_payment (lines 1017-1034 for write, 1236-1252 for read), BEFORE the request actually succeeds. The documented contract ('the access fee is spent... the request is served', line 1305) is violated on several paths: (1) handle_put calls enforce_write_ctx (1713) — which debits — and only afterwards runs the lockout guard that can return 409 (1736) and validate_rdf_body that can return 400 (1742) and storage.put which can fail; a rejected write still cost sats. (2) handle_post with an `.acl` Slug calls enforce_write_ctx twice (1803 on the container, then 1835 on the resolved sidecar) — a paid container is charged, potentially twice. (3) handle_get charges at enforce_read_ctx (1461) but then may return 404 (1629) for a resource that does not exist — paying for nothing; the container text/html path also calls enforce_read_ctx twice (1461 and 1482). (4) handle_copy charges the destination write (2923) before the source read authorisation (2951) can deny the whole COPY. In every case the caller loses satoshis on a request that is refused, errors, or does not exist.

## Recommendation

Separate the balance CHECK (in the authz gate) from the DEBIT, and perform the debit only once, after the request has fully succeeded (validation passed, storage write committed, 2xx determined). For read, debit only when bytes are actually served (not on 404). For COPY, authorise source+destination before any charge.

title: [MEDIUM] Proxy forwards X-Upstream-Authorization across cross-origin and HTTPS->HTTP redirects
description:
**File:** [`crates/solid-pod-rs-server/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/solid-pod-rs/blob/fix/acl-candidate-control/blob/fix/crates/solid-pod-rs-server/src/lib.rs#L3330-L3359) (lines 3330, 3336, 3359)
**Project:** solid-pod-acl-control
**Severity:** MEDIUM  •  **Confidence:** medium  •  **Slug:** `other-credential-leak`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `noreply@anthropic.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

handle_proxy forwards the caller-supplied X-Upstream-Authorization header as the outbound Authorization header (lines 3330-3336) on EVERY hop of its manual redirect loop. Because redirects are followed manually (redirect::Policy::none, 3274) and current_url is simply replaced with the redirect target (3359) before looping, the same Authorization value is re-sent to the redirect target without checking that the target host/scheme matches the original. A first-hop server that is on the SSRF allowlist (any public host) can therefore 30x-redirect to an attacker-controlled public host and harvest the upstream credential, or redirect from https:// to http:// causing the bearer token to be transmitted in cleartext. reqwest's built-in redirect handling strips Authorization on cross-origin redirects precisely to prevent this; the manual loop reintroduces the leak. Only authenticated pod users can invoke the proxy, but the leaked secret is their upstream API credential.

## Recommendation

When following a redirect, drop the forwarded Authorization header unless the redirect target has the same origin (scheme+host+port) as the request that carried it, and refuse to forward it over an https->http downgrade. Reusing reqwest's default redirect policy (with per-hop SSRF re-validation) would also inherit its header-stripping.

title: [MEDIUM] /.well-known/apps publishes per-pod manifest.json bypassing WAC
description:
**File:** [`crates/solid-pod-rs-server/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/solid-pod-rs/blob/fix/acl-candidate-control/blob/fix/crates/solid-pod-rs-server/src/lib.rs#L4658-L4676) (lines 4658, 4664, 4676)
**Project:** solid-pod-acl-control
**Severity:** MEDIUM  •  **Confidence:** medium  •  **Slug:** `acl-check`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `noreply@anthropic.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

handle_well_known_apps (public, no auth) iterates every pod directory under data_root and reads `{pod}/apps/manifest.json` directly from disk via tokio::fs::read (lines 4658-4676), returning the contents to any anonymous caller, with the pod owner's pubkey injected (4670-4674). This read goes straight to the filesystem and never calls enforce_read_ctx, so a manifest the pod owner has protected with a restrictive ACL (e.g. an app config under a private container) is still published. Enumeration of pods/pubkeys is by design (JSS #464), but serving a WAC-protected resource's bytes without evaluating its ACL is an authorization bypass / information disclosure.

## Recommendation

Resolve each manifest through the Storage + WAC path (enforce_read_ctx for an anonymous principal) and include only manifests an anonymous client is actually granted Read on, rather than reading them straight from disk.

title: [BUG] SPARQL DELETE/INSERT ... WHERE applies templates unconditionally (WHERE ignored)
description:
**File:** [`crates/solid-pod-rs/src/ldp.rs`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/solid-pod-rs/blob/fix/acl-candidate-control/blob/fix/crates/solid-pod-rs/src/ldp.rs#L1442-L1450) (lines 1442, 1443, 1449, 1450) **Project:** solid-pod-acl-control **Severity:** BUG • **Confidence:** medium • **Slug:** `other-logic-bug` ## Owners **Suggested assignee:** `github@xrsystems.uk` _(via last-committer)_ ## Finding apply_sparql_patch handles GraphUpdateOperation::DeleteInsert with `{ delete, insert, .. }`, discarding the parsed WHERE group graph pattern. The delete templates (when fully ground) are removed and the insert templates (when fully ground) are added with no evaluation of the WHERE clause against the target graph. A SPARQL-Update such as `DELETE {

} INSERT { } WHERE { }` will delete and insert even though the WHERE precondition matches nothing. This diverges from SPARQL 1.1 Update semantics (DeleteInsert is conditional on WHERE bindings) and from the N3 PATCH path in the same file, which correctly enforces its `where` block (lines 1170-1181) and returns PreconditionFailed on a miss. Effect is silent, incorrect graph mutation / potential loss of triples the client intended to keep. Patterns containing variables are instead silently skipped (ground conversion returns None), so variable-bearing DELETE WHERE / DELETE INSERT becomes a no-op — a second correctness surprise. Not an attacker-reachable security issue (the mutation is scoped to the resource the caller is already authorised to write via enforce_write_ctx), hence a non-security bug. ## Recommendation Either reject DeleteInsert operations that carry a non-trivial WHERE pattern with PodError::Unsupported (matching the pod's documented 'no WHERE-clause resolution for PATCH' limitation), or implement WHERE evaluation and gate the delete/insert on it. At minimum, do not destructure away `pattern` with `..` and silently proceed; detect a present WHERE and fail closed so a conditional update never mutates unconditionally. ## Recent committers (`git log`) - Dr John O'Hare (2026-10-29) - Claude Code (2026-10-19) - jjohare (2026-07-10)
